newsitem.title: USA: Most US stock index futures reverse losses, end up.
newsitem.headline: Most US stock index futures reverse losses, end up.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed mostly higher, reversing the day's losses in a fresh flush of mutual fund money, traders and analysts said.
"You are seeing a lot of money out there going directly to stocks," one futures trader said.
"That's what the market has seen before -- huge inflows into stock indexes," another trader said.

Signs that investors were pouring more money into the U.S. stock market in December through the first week of Janaury overrode any concerns about higher U.S. interest rates. Theoretically, higher rates make U.S. stocks less attractive.
"I think you saw a divergence," said Jack Bouroudjian, vice president of equity derivatives at Credit Agricole. "I don't think we are following interest rates anymore."
Bouroudjian said the stock market on a second look interpreted the sharp rise in nonfarm payrolls and the decline in unemployment as positive for U.S. corporate earnings.
"This is exactly what the market needed," he said. "We needed to see a good growth rate without any inflation."
The U.S. labor data pointed to fourth-quarter GDP growth of 4.0 percent, sparking inflation fears and pushing yields on the Treasury's 30-year bond sharply higher.
March Standard & Poor's 500s initially fell in reaction to the bond market's strong reaction to the data, but stocks overall steadily inched higher on dealer and fund buying.
"This is all 401(K) money," another trader said.
Many traders were encouraged by recent reports showing that billions of dollars of mutual fund money continued to flow into U.S. stocks in the last month of the year.
The buying frenzy by fund and portfolio managers culminated in a final rush before the weekend. March tested the one-month high and all-time settlement high of 767.00 in the final minutes of trade.

Light arbitrage buy programs were noted at about a 6.05 point premium to cash. Fair value is at 5.15 points, and arbitrage sell programs were touched off earlier when March's premium to cash narrowed to 4.25 points, traders said.
Gains in S&P futures finally spilled into the Nikkei futures pit where March briefly traded above the 1,000-point lower trading limit. March Nikkeis spent most of the day locked limit-down.
March Nikkeis closed at the contract low of 17,265, down 1,000 points.

At the end of pit trade, March S&Ps were up 7.70 at 766.60, KCBT Value Lines were up 6.05 at 699.20, New Composites were up 3.95 at 404.70, Midcap 400s were 2.15 higher at 264.00 and Nasdaq 100s jumped 11.00 to 876.00 ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
